justification: Refresh requires holding and precisely releasing at an 80px commit threshold; early release snaps back with no result and no one-tap alternative — basic action made needlessly difficult (interaction friction).

UI in English, explicitly disclosed; easy cancel; identical content to B variant — no manipulation.

Predictable rewards disclosed ('predictable 3–6 coins — no slot-machine suspense'); no streak pressure.
Equal visual weight (ratio 1.0); data sharing off by default, privacy-preserving option on; honest descriptions.

Fees ($6.50 processing + $3.25 service) hidden behind a tiny grey text line; no total shown; button says only 'Book ticket' — drip pricing.
Variable-ratio reward ('35% nothing, 10% jackpot — dopamine on a schedule'), streak-loss fear ('Don't lose your streak'), and 'resets soon' urgency.

Pull-To-Refresh §1 (kinesthetic resistance/commit): R_elastic>0 ('Elastic resistance builds as you pull') + τ_commit=80px; releasing early snaps back with no result — refresh requires sustained physical effort to a precise threshold, no one-tap alternative.
Bad Defaults §1 (pre-initialized activation): both checkboxes State(·,t₀)=True with zero user events ('Pre-checked at t₀'); §3 (intent): labels map to marketing opt-in & privacy-loss domains.
Wrong Language §2/§3: L_DOM=English matches session language, explicitly disclosed ('Everything you see here is in English'); no critical node in a foreign language; cancel affordance present.

Forced Continuity §1 (time-triggered silent mutation): S_trial with cached token T_payment (Visa ••••4242) — transition to S_premium + charge at t_expiry without explicit conversion consent; §2: no renewal warning rendered in fair-notice window; only 'advance to t_expiry' affordance.
Small/Moving Close Button §2 (microscopic hitbox): A(close)=44×44px ≥ WCAG minimum τ_wcag_hitbox; §3: accessible name 'Close dialog' — no trigger.
Small/Moving Close Button §2: A(close)=8×8px < 44×44px WCAG minimum (min-width/min-height 0), faded at 30% opacity — microscopic, near-invisible dismissal vector.
Customisation §3 (jargon obfuscation): labels are plain language with explanations ('Ads based on what you browse on this site'); §1/§2: no nesting asymmetry.
Friend Spam §2 (granular selection): message targets only the 3 user-selected contacts; §3 (sender spoofing): message 'clearly branded as coming from PopSocial' — no identity spoofing.

Watch Ads §1 (attention as currency): ad completion is sole unlock token; §3 (semantic inflation): 'EXCLUSIVE/AMAZING/PREMIUM LEGENDARY', '0.01% drop rate' hype for a loot crate — hype-utility divergence.
Framing §2 (visual weight): renew and cancel buttons carry identical styling/weight; §1: no subtree embellishment asymmetry; consequences of cancelling disclosed.
Drip Pricing §2 (visual disparity): fees itemized at normal weight with total $58.75 on the button ('all-inclusive'); §3: fee terms present above the fold — no concealment.

Countdown Timer §1 (stateless expiration): 00:15 timer tethered to page load; §3 (urgency inflation): 'Hurry — only guaranteed while the timer runs'; plus auto-confirm at 00:00 (Automating-the-user-away §1: action executes with E_user=∅ at t≥τ_system).
Wrong Language §2/§3: content identical to B — all English, disclosed, easy cancel; no locale mismatch or foreign-language critical node.

Trick Questions §1 (label-input semantic mismatch): aria-label 'Opt me out of the newsletter' vs visual label 'Keep me subscribed' — semantic opposites (double-bind); §2: checking box maps to inclusion intent contrary to aria semantics.

Framing §2 (visual weight asymmetry): renew CTA py-3.5/bold/shadow-lg vs cancel at text-[8px] muted/40% underline link; §1: gain subtree carries heavy embellishment vs loss subtree — opt-out visually demoted.
Addictive Design §3 (reinforcement-lexicon density): explicitly 'predictable 3–6 coins each — no slot-machine suspense'; no variable-ratio schedule, no streak-loss pressure.
Privacy Zuckering §2 (visual asymmetry): 'visual weight ratio = 1.0 — identical hitboxes, contrast, accent saturation'; sharing OFF by default, preserving ON — no skew.

Customisation §3 (jargon obfuscation): 'jargon ratio 0.93', technical labels ('cross-device graph linkage', 'programmatic data monetisation') with 'no plain-language explanation'; plus Bad Defaults §1/§3: 3 of 5 privacy options pre-checked at t₀.

Drip Pricing §2 (visual disparity): base price text-[20px] bold vs fees at text-[8px] light-grey rgb(185,185,185) behind a clickable line; §1: no total anywhere, button says only 'Book ticket' — cost hidden until interaction.

Addictive Design §3: dense reinforcement lexicon ('claim your daily bonus', 'streak: 12 days', 'level up 3 XP away', 'spin again', 'don't lose your streak') + explicit variable-ratio schedule ('35% nothing, 10% jackpot — dopamine on a schedule').

Automatic Accept §2 (opaque entity resolution): all recipients named (Acme Analytics, Beacon Metrics, Coral Data) with purposes; 'complete list — no unnamed recipients, E_declared = E_actual' — no trigger.

Disguised Ad §2 (morphological similarity): ad card reuses native article layout/classes (gradient icon block, headline, excerpt, byline); 'AD' tag only 7px at 40% opacity in corner — blends with editorial content.
Pre-Delivered Content §3: assets framed as 'delivered with your purchase and already on this device', badges 'Installed' — not reframed as purchase opportunities; no locked-content density (§2).
Trick Questions §1: aria-label 'Keep me subscribed to the weekly newsletter' matches visual label exactly — no semantic mismatch.
Watch Ads §3 (semantic inflation): honest framing ('1 cosmetic sticker, no gameplay effect'), no hyperbole; §2 no progress misrepresentation — informed attention exchange.
Countdown Timer §1/§3: timer present but 'nothing auto-confirms' and explicit anti-urgency text ('Take the time you need — the offer stands') — no synthetic pressure.
Bad Defaults §1: 'Everything below is optional and starts unchecked' — no pre-initialized activation at t₀.
Feedforward Ambiguity §1/§3: 'Step 2 of 2 — final confirmation', button 'Place order — $89.00' matches outcome; Expect=Resolve — no divergence.
Automatic Accept §2 (opaque entity resolution): consent to unnamed 'trusted partners' — vague umbrella, E_declared≈0; §1: no decoupling toggle; §3: 'by continuing, you agree…' auto-accepted.

Feedforward Ambiguity §1/§3: 'Step 2 of 3 — one more step after this one' + non-descriptive 'Continue' button; expected outcome (place order, review summary shown) diverges from actual (another step) — Expect≠Resolve.
Friend Spam §3 (sender identity spoofing): message 'sent as your personal invite' — user identity injected into sender alias of corporate message; §2 not triggered (3 contacts selected).
Pull-To-Refresh §1: one-tap 'Refresh feed' button, 'no resistance, no threshold' — no kinesthetic resistance or commit threshold.
Choice Overload §1 (excessive quantization): 30 distinct add-on toggles in one decision context (>τ_overload≈20); §2: high interactive density in cramped scrollable grid with truncated labels.

Privacy Zuckering §2 (visual asymmetry): W(invasive)/W(preserving)=3.6>τ_privacy_skew — sharing option larger/saturated/pre-set ON vs preserving small/dim/OFF; §1 bundled default toward data surrender.
Disguised Ad §2: ad visually separated (dashed amber border, 'Sponsored' pill + megaphone icon, 'ad · third-party' label) — morphological differentiation, no mimicry.
Pre-Delivered Content §3: assets already local on device (paths shown) reframed as 'Premium add-ons ready to download' with fake scarcity 'grab them before they're gone'.
Choice Overload §1: 30 options decomposed into 3 collapsible categories (≤10 per decision context) — cognitive load managed.
Forced Continuity §1/§2: identical to A — trial with cached payment token for time-triggered charge, no renewal warning, no cancel affordance.
